name: Dwight Yoakam
notes: The Bakersfield revival's commercial engine, and the only artist entry in this section the research rates Confidence: high — "a stripped-down approach to traditional honky tonk and Bakersfield country" built on a shuffled two-beat, a Telecaster and a nasal tenor. The drum numbers come from the sourced Bakersfield reading, "a big drum beat" with "heavy use of electric instrumentation and backbeats": the velocity tiers sit at 110–127 accent over a 78–96 main, which is a harder, more forward backbeat than the genre's 104–127 over 74–92. The kick is the entry's documented two-beat on 1 and 3 "opening to quarters on the dancehall cuts", so densityPerBar runs 2–4 against the genre's 2–3. The lope is stated to live on a tight hi-hat rather than the ride, which is why the inherited ride lane (percs) drops to 0–2 hits at −10 dB and the open hat falls to 0.10. BPM 73–170 is the entry's own band, with its mid-shuffle cluster 91–126, fast dancehall 138–170 and weepers 73–97; mode 107 is the entry's "Ain't That Lonely Yet" reading. Harmony is the entry's own list — I–IV–V with V7, the I–I7–IV turn, twelve-bar frames on the barroom cuts, and a ii–V turnaround at the eight-bar boundary — with the sevenths expressed in extensions because a numeral names a degree, not a quality. Melody is the documented "high, lonesome twang" and "sweetly nasal tenor": narrow range, hard consonant attack (staccato), the signature catch on phrase ends (endVariation) and minimal melisma. The countermelody is Pete Anderson's lead guitar, which the source compares to Don Rich — "a second lead voice in stinging single-note and double-stop lines, not a chordal accompanist" — so answer_lick carries the weight at a high density ratio. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are swing.amount 0.66, every velocity tier, the ghost probability and positions, hihat.fillDensity and the percs density: the research gives tempo bands and the words "big", "tight" and "hard", and the section's own swing-ratio table (2:1–3:1 at 100–135 BPM) is marked [LOW-CONF] on its percentage conversions by its own author. ⚠ The per-track BPM readings are bpmdatabase values and are [LOW-CONF] as a class in the research. ⚠ era is written 1990-2016 because the entry documents two windows — 1990–2002 (the Pete Anderson production era) and 2012–2016 (self-produced) — and this model covers both. The documented Tex-Mex polka variant and the 2016 drummerless bluegrass re-orchestration are real alternate lanes but are deliberately NOT authored as modes, because authoring modes would delete the three moods this model inherits from country-shuffle.
